brief: 2026 was a derating year: the S&P 500 forward P/E fell even as EPS grew ~33%, driven by AI monetization/regulatory concerns, a spike in yields and credit spreads, higher oil, and a drop in net buybacks. History favors a reversal: after >10% P/E declines, SPX has returned a median 20% the next year. UBS keeps its end-2027 S&P 500 target at 8900 (18x 2028 EPS of $490) and sets 9600 for end-2028, forecasting 18% EPS growth in 2027 and 14% in 2028, with NVDA, MU and AVGO alone ~45% of 2027's earnings growth. A new risk from the midterms: state-level pauses put ~30% of 2028 data center capacity additions at risk, with policy details unknown until next year. Strategy: buy derated AI Semis and Software as cloud revenue growth nearly tripled Q1-to-Q3 and AI revenue potential (~$2.5tr) clears the ~$2tr capex hurdle; buy Healthcare over Staples and Financials/cyclicals over bond-proxy defensives as the expansion continues; favor balance-sheet strength as the Fed hikes twice more; expect net buybacks to rebound $200-400bn next year as hyperscaler cash flow recovers from capex-driven share issuance.
